question: Can effect operations read a previously drawn VS code allocation, and which bytes must an equivalent readback expose?

scope.qualification: Static activation that holds only under conditions, and a byte-observation contract. No runtime call frequency, full set of escaped pointers or draw acceptance is established.

dependencies.use: Defines the preserved copy and recreation reader and the independent cache and lifetime observations.
Defines the selector, persistent and inline destination, cache and stamp branches.
Defines ordered sparse patch writes and their input and extent qualifications.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground serial read-only native-word, raw direct-BL and literal-pointer queries through tools/run-headless.ps1, corroborated by narrow exact-function generated windows. Direct BL and literal-pointer inventories exclude computed or CTR entry points; sparse database xrefs prove no absence.

inputQualification.qualification: 470 differing bytes in60 ranges were confined to [0x827F3F50,0x827F4280). Cited semantic words avoid that band. Checkout revision is not generated-byte provenance.

effectOwnership.constructor: 0x825E8A80 builds a340-byte effect object O and installs vptr 0x8207C768 at 0x825E8A9C; initialized slot+0x18 at 0x8207C780 contains 0x8265F6D8.
effectOwnership.layout: O+0x18 points to 24-byte shader records Q; O+0x48 points to 108-byte effect entries E. Selected descriptor and value indices link these tables. Q+4 is a D3D resource, Q+8 its preserved byte buffer and Q+0x14 its flags.
effectOwnership.recordProduction: 0x825E0388 limits the record index by O+0x14 and creates buffer Q+8. Type 16 selects VS and type 15 PS. 0x825E0248 obtains buffer bytes, calls CreateVS 0x826945E8 at 0x825E0290 and stores Q+4 at 0x825E0294; success sets Q+0x14 bits 0xC0000000.
effectOwnership.drawIdentity: 0x8265D778 stores a selected Q pointer in a 32-byte runtime state at 0x8265D95C. State dispatcher 0x8266B370 type 10 loads Q+4 at 0x8266BA1C and calls SetVS 0x82692C48 at 0x8266BA20, tying this same resource to G+0x3198.

activation.preparationClient: 0x825E1C40 has two raw BL callers: 0x825E465C in effect setup 0x825E44E8 and 0x8266B27C in pass-state preparation 0x8266B1F0. Setup selects E+0xC bit 0x02000000; pass preparation selects 0x08000000; both require E+0x20 != 0xFFFF. Effect loaders 0x8257FEB8 and 0x82580200 and clone 0x8265F808 call setup. Pass preparation also has state-dispatch and BeginPass-shaped 0x8266C530 entry point.
activation.queryClient: 0x8265DFB0 recurses at 0x8265E1A8 and is called at 0x8265F788 by installed description-query slot 0x8265F6D8. Its selected shader path exposes VS bytes at output+8 and PS bytes at output+0xC. Semantic API names are descriptive inferences, not recovered retail symbols.
activation.copyPredicate: Both clients require Q+0x14 bit 0x80000000 and nonnull Q+4 before calling 0x82662D28 at 0x825E1D2C and 0x8265E26C; successful refresh clears that dirty bit. Repeated pass and query invocation therefore need not copy. Initial loading may copy before any draw.
activation.afterDrawWitness: Same-device clone 0x8265F808 compares devices at 0x8265F870..0x8265F888, shares and AddRefs source Q+4 into destination Q+4 at 0x8265FAC4, ORs 0x80000000 into destination Q+0x14 at 0x8265FB00 and calls setup 0x825E44E8 at 0x8265FB34. Under preserved resource identity and lifetime this can read a VS already patched by a draw without an intervening draw.
activation.frequency: Load, clone, pass application and descriptor-query events are established static contexts. Caller-controlled frequency and actual post-draw instance and order are unobserved; no unconditional per-frame copy is established.

byteFate.copy: Nonnull destination in 0x82694480 copies metadata from VS+0x368 for M=word(VS+0x36C), then S=word(VS+0x370) code bytes from C=word(VS+0x20) to destination+M. Null destination only reports M+S. The cache and variant prefix is excluded.
byteFate.recreation: 0x82662D28 retains the result in Q+8. Device mismatch at 0x82662E08 releases Q+4 and recreates through 0x825E0248. Copied patched code can become both new code and constructor-saved fetch input, so another draw is not proved to repair stale or differently patched input.
byteFate.otherConsumers: 0x825E1C40 passes selected copied bytes to reflection and chunk helpers 0x8265BC20 at 0x825E1EC0 and 0x82580460 at 0x825E1F58. Their local format-dependent reads are limited as described below; description query exposes a buffer pointer. External output consumers and whether any consumer keeps the pointer remain unclosed.

equivalentReadback.requiredBytes: At a reached nonnull copy, expose C*(t): the entire resource-generation code range as the Original would have left it immediately before the copy. Start with creation bytes and replay ordered persistent sparse writes, preserving untouched bytes and ordered overlap across variants, consumed calls and preserved or fallback Originals.
equivalentReadback.branchHistory: A compatible ADC48 cache hit writes no C, even if the most recent draw key differs. A reusable miss patches C through AD150. Busy miss or forced inline uses ADA38 and patches ring storage, leaving C unchanged. No-in-flight removes no forced-inline branch from byte 2ABE/2ABC high bits. ADD88 can patch primary and variant 1 in one invocation; one last key is insufficient.
equivalentReadback.minimalScopedBridge: Before the nonnull copy at 0x82694480, materialize missing C* bytes and execute the existing copy. An implementation that saves, materializes, copies and restores additionally needs disjoint output, code and metadata storage and no concurrent or reentrant observer or writer. The null size query needs no materialization.
equivalentReadback.sideEffects: This scoped copy alone needs no variant tag, stride or stamp stores and no G+0x2E38 stores. Logical tag, stride and ID history is needed to predict Original branch choices. Stamp reuse modeling is separate; do not manufacture an extra publication stamp. Independent setter and lifetime readers retain their own obligations.
equivalentReadback.durableMaterialization: Leaving C* in place also requires coherence with every future Original cache decision. Old tag and stride prefixes can otherwise accept changed bytes as a compatible hit. Maintain logical cache history and synchronize, intercept or refuse before Original execution; readback-only prefix omission is not a durable-cache proof.
equivalentReadback.refusal: Refuse consumption before losing history if resource generation, immutable patch inputs, exact code extents, alias protection, branch and cache history or future Original coherence cannot be established.

consumerInspection.qualification: V: Only the complete local bodies 0x82580460..0x825805A0 and 0x8265BC20..0x8265BF34 were newly expanded. Their279 native words matched the supported flat image outside the mismatch band. The BC20 decompiler stopped at its save thunk; full raw words and exact generated windows supplied interpretation. Generated revision is checkout identity, not generation provenance.
consumerInspection.chunkFinder: V: 0x82580460 clears optional pointer and length outputs first. Null input returns 0x8876086C. Header mask 0x102A1100 returns 1 without scanning. Other accepted high16 families 0x4658/0x5458/0x7FFE/0x7FFF/0xFFFE/0xFFFF scan token words from B+4. A low16=0xFFFE token with k=(word>>16)&0x7FFF greater than 1 compares the next word to the requested tag; match returns payload pointer T+8 and length 4*(k-1), return 0. Low16=0xFFFF returns 1; unsupported header returns 0x88760B59. Skips depend on token and header bits; no input-length bound or termination proof exists. Traversed token and tag words can affect results; skipped payload is not read locally.
consumerInspection.reflection: V: 0x8265BC20 initializes three 8-byte halfword groups and pointer and optional length outputs. For header mask 0x102A1100 it selects D=word(B+0x10), C=B+D+4, L=word(B+D), unless D=0. Other headers call 0x82580460 at 0x8265BCF0 with tag 0x42415443. Signed-negative helper results become return 0; null selected C also returns 0. Selected chunks require L>=28 and the unsigned wrapped count test L>=4*(word(C+0xC)+7). It reads entry offset word(C+0x10), 20-byte entries, NUL name bytes with a bounded read, register-set, base and count halfwords at entry+0x4/+0x6/+0x8, optional default-offset word at entry+0x10, and repeatedly reloads the count. It updates four sum, min and max groups, then publishes C/L. It checks default offset plus count*width but never dereferences default-value bytes. Validation failure returns 0x80004005 without rolling back aggregates.
consumerInspection.dependence: I: Metadata-only independence needs the actual selected ranges disjoint from persistent patch writes, stable readable inputs and protected output, frame and lifetime aliases. No complete-buffer validation or universal code independence follows. Selected pointers and non-specialized readback output remain guest-visible; unexpanded external users may retain or process them. No local hash or file call establishes absence in those users.

bridgeAlternatives.orderedHistory: I: Option(a) is exact only when generation-specific C* and logical selector, cache, ID and lifetime transitions include every consumed and preserved Original operation. Materialize before every actual code reader, including ADA38 current-code copying; cover prefix and key readers separately. A94480-only hook supplies only the scoped copy portion.
bridgeAlternatives.lazyPatch: I: Option(b) reconstructed from the latest key fails on compatible hits, inline nonwrites, other-variant and ordered overlap histories. Full-history lazy materialization reduces to (a). Durable code writes require coherent future Original tag, key and stamp decisions; scoped save, copy and restore requires exclusion and disjointness. Neither a synthetic stamp nor a G+0x2E38-only publication is justified.
bridgeAlternatives.readerRefusal: I: Option(c) needs a generation, lifetime and alias eligibility proof before the first lost patch, including future acquisitions such as clone and escaped byte pointers. Current dirty bits, raw address, refcount or effect affiliation alone do not decide that temporal predicate. No exact executable live-reader predicate is established in the selected implementation; conservative refusal must precede history loss.
bridgeAlternatives.compactImage: I: Option(d) refines the existing C* representation: retain creation bytes and apply persistent sparse writes immediately in Original order to a per-generation image or byte overlay. Induction preserves the same byte result without an unbounded event log; untouched bytes and duplicate or overlapping destinations remain significant. State is O(S) for a full S-byte image plus logical state, update work O(w) for w bytes written, and non-specialized readback still copies M+S bytes. These are bounds, not measured cost. Direct output synthesis might avoid guest overlay writes only after exact alias, ordering, ABI and fault and complete-reader coverage is proved.
bridgeAlternatives.recommendation: I: Prefer (a) with (d) compact current-image storage and reader interception, on the condition that all existing refusal guards are kept until generation, branch and state coverage, and alias and Original coherence are proved. This is a research contract, not draw acceptance or a claim that reader frequency makes it worthwhile.

shippedInteraction.dirtyReplay: V: indexed_buffer_consume.cpp:340 zeros five qwords G+0x0..0x27. UP then stores qword 1 at G+0x18 as word(G+0x18)=0 and word(G+0x1C)=1. Notifications at indexed_buffer_consume.cpp:375 and user_pointer_consume.cpp:245 precede replay. I: Bridge input and history capture must precede loss of entry state; reader reachability does not undo or replace those effects.
shippedInteraction.identityMemo: V: solid_draw_adapter.cpp:791 uses 256 thread-local slots; hashes locate entries and exact equality of 13 byte spans validates current-draw derived code. indexed_buffer_draw_inputs.cpp:669 reads current patch inputs with optional exact-byte journal validation at:462. Neither facility retains Original generation history or publishes guest code or cache state. native_draw_shader_words.cpp:60 requires both VS and PS; its no-PS patch-model limit does not describe every other host reader. I: A logical overlay must provide a consistent view to cache validation and derivation; memo code with inline linkage is not persistent C*.
shippedInteraction.watch: V: vs_code_watch.cpp:17 declares default-off, init-only observation; :151 disables raw views and shader read cache and installs guarded copies. vs_code_probe.cpp:25 compares selected current guest code with expected current fetch backing; :78 compares current 16 stream bytes against G+0x2E38 and selected Rv+0x30. It does not compare tag, allocation and stamp history or observe guest loads. :182 independently drains event counts; stale shader addresses are cumulative and capped at 256, not generation identities. These counters measure exposure, not reader cadence.
shippedInteraction.remainingObservation: I: Proposed reader-entry events need call and root, generation, frame, epoch and thread, Qdirty, size and copy, bytes, and clone and query ordering. Separate transition events need both variants, hit, miss, busy and inline outcomes, actual destinations, ID, tag, key and stamp values, and preserved Original divergence. Coverage drops, escaped aliases, overlap, reentry and unreadable cases must be explicit. Counters can measure sampled frequency and cost but cannot prove universal alias or future-reader absence; no new counter or runtime result is asserted.

generationReaderLedgerBoundary.qualification: Static event and reader obligations that hold only under conditions; no runtime population, full set of alias paths, model validation or consume acceptance.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.notation: PCs/device offsets/masks are hexadecimal; U reduces modulo32; W/Q are BE32/BE64. Rv=VS+0x1A0*v,C=W(VS+0x20),M=W(VS+0x36C),S=W(VS+0x370). Resource header+0x08 lifetime differs from Rv+0x40 reuse stamp; VD+0x30 is the declaration ID. Byte counts and explicitly decimal stack arguments retain their units.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.readerScope: The supported readback, reflection, acquisition and lifetime, setter, preserved helper and host cached-read families remain separate boundaries; copied buffers retain the snapshot they received.
requiredEventKinds: executed sparse payload and overlap order
global atomic IDs and key/cache publication
refresh/buffer/outer activation and transient Q state
host actual reads and journal/memo/watch validity
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.sparseWriteSite: At 0x826AD720 read patch index; 0x826AD72C sets r3=r22+12*(index&0xFFF); 0x826AD730/0x826AD734 skip exact equality with scratch r31; 0x826AD738 sets r5=12, 0x826AD73C r4=r31; 0x826AD740 calls 0x827F8550. Capture final 12 bytes, destination and skips in executed list order, preserving duplicates and overlaps and shared primary and secondary code.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.atomicPublicationSites: Global 0x82FA0544: 0x826ADD30 reservation load, 0x826ADD34 increment, 0x826ADD38 conditional store, 0x826ADD40 retry to 0x826ADD28; 0x826ADD44/48/4C rejects candidates FFFFFFFF and 0 via 0x826ADD24. 0x826ADD50 stores VD ID, 0x826ADD58 tag, 0x826ADD60/68 record strides, 0x826ADD78/7C device caches. Preserve MSR and reservation outcomes and global interleaving; no finite contention bound is proved.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.stampSites: Non-specialized 0x826AE5AC loads actual G+0x2A9C, 0x826AE5B0 stores selected Rv+0x40, 0x826AE5B4 publishes cursor after packet writes. Z stamps 0x826AE414/0x826AE498/0x826AE508 precede cursor 0x826AE530. ADC48 and readback do not independently publish a stamp; issue, completed, B, RPTR and host generations remain distinct.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.inlineSource: ADA38 at 0x826ADB08 copies L current persistent source bytes through its encoded alias; 0x826ADB18 cache call covers SOURCE(A,U(A+L),0), then optional linkage and 0x826ADB6C fetch patch precede cursor and reversed G+0x2E40/G+0x2E38 cache publication. General L, alias, cache, helper and storage lifetime remain qualified.
generationReaderLedgerBoundary.partialCurrentObservers: The raw AD150 wrapper saves selected entry operands, runs Original and optionally reads after-images; 0x826AE5B8 selection observer can read selected code after non-specialized stamp and cursor. Solid readers use 132 bytes; label and active capture use selected metadata lengths. These are genuine optional host readers and partial coverage, not ordered patch and global-ID history. Lowerer entry and pre-take samples and scalar readback entry and return samples do not supply a generation certificate.

scalarReaderObserver.qualification: The source-bound reader observer at 0x82662D28 and 0x82694480 saves entry operands, scalar Q, header and query-size fields and raw return values with pairing and loss quality. It samples no code payload, metadata payload, patch history or state history and explicitly leaves allocation generation and outer activation unknown. Source inspection alone establishes no review or runtime acceptance or installed-main coverage.
scalarReaderObserver.scalarReads: Refresh samples saved Q+0x04/Q+0x08/Q+0x14 and O+0x0C at entry and normal return. Query samples metadata and code sizes at entry and the saved size-output pointer at normal return; copy samples sizes and code pointer at entry, with no exit memory read. Raw entry operands and results and pairing and quality records do not supply payload or intermediate-write history.

generationReaderLedgerBoundary.fixtureContract: A successful allocation-generation baseline, immutable effective inputs before loss, actual ordered Original writes and branches and independent full-state and byte expectations are required. Global ID attempts, actual issue and completion stamp domains, escaped aliases and all permitted concurrent observers and writers need coverage. Unknown target, generation or input, dropped events or ambiguous ordering invalidate the affected interval; finite zero counts prove no universal completeness.

nextDiscriminator: Link actual descriptor-slot callers and output+8 consumers; identify concrete selected chunk or range and buffer dispatch targets before claiming code independence, alias protection or absence of hashing, comparison or persistence beyond the inspected helpers.
Link actual resource generation and order, patch-input snapshots and Original branch history before implementing an exact readback bridge.
Prove scoped alias and reentrancy guards or durable code and cache coherence before selecting a materialization policy.
guards: Do not equate raw caller counts with runtime frequency or the static clone example with an observed clone.
Do not reconstruct code from only the last consumed key, patch inline draws into persistent C, or assume a subsequent draw repairs recreation from different saved input.
Do not infer draw acceptance, complete API equivalence or universal prefix deadness from this byte-observation contract.
conclusion: Effect preparation and installed description queries retain code readback; same-device cloning supplies an identity-preserving post-draw activation that holds only under conditions. An equivalent bridge must expose ordered Original persistent-code history, with scoped copy and durable cache coherence treated separately.
